children: Circle says it generated roughly $1.4 billion in first-half 2026 revenue while spending $819 million on distribution partners and related costs. The disclosure highlights the expense of building a widely used stablecoin payment network.
Circle’s USDC business is generating substantial revenue, but its latest disclosures show how much of that income is needed to support distribution and infrastructure.

The stablecoin issuer reported approximately $1.4 billion of revenue in the first half of 2026. It said around $819 million went to partners and transaction-related costs, while another $473 million supported operational, compliance and technology spending.
That leaves a much smaller proportion of revenue as retained profit than the headline size of USDC might suggest.
The Economics Of A Digital Dollar
Circle holds reserves backing USDC in cash and highly liquid financial instruments. Those assets can produce interest income, creating an important revenue stream for the issuer.
But USDC’s usefulness depends on its presence across exchanges, wallets, payment services and other financial applications.
Those distribution arrangements can be expensive. Coinbase is among Circle’s most important commercial partners, reflecting its role in making the stablecoin accessible to users.
As NewsBTC has previously explained, USDC aims to maintain its value against the dollar while remaining transferable across supported networks.
New stablecoin issuers and conventional financial institutions are entering the market. They will compete not only on the reliability of their reserves but also on distribution, redemption and cost.
Circle’s revenue also depends partly on interest rates. Lower yields on reserves could compress income even if USDC’s circulation remains relatively strong.

The latest figures reveal an important part of the stablecoin business: issuing the digital dollar may be only the first step. The partners enabling people to use it can command a considerable share of the economic value.
Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Circle Reveals $819 Million USDC Payouts As Stablecoin Economics Come Under Scrutiny
